newsitem.title: USA: Loewen edges up on bid, long fight seen.
newsitem.headline: Loewen edges up on bid, long fight seen.

text.p: Shares of Loewen Group Inc edged up slightly after rival Service Corp International launched a hostile takeover, but Wall Street takeover traders said the prospects of a long battle prevented the stock from rising closer to the $45 bid level.
"It's going to take a long time to get this moving along," said one arbitrageuer.
Shares of Loewen, which began trading on the NYSE Wednesday stood at 42-1/2 in the U.S., up from Tuesday's Nasdaq close of 42-1/16.

Service Corp earlier launched an exchange offer valued at $45 per share, or about $2.9 billion. The move followed Loewen's rejection last week of an unsolicited offer valued at $43 per share, or $2.8 billion.

Arbitrageurs also noted Service Corp faces a huge hurdle in winning 75 percent of outstanding shares, as required by the offer. Loewen chairman Ray Loewen holds about 15 percent of the company's stock and other insiders hold another five percent.
"For (Loewen) to even begin looking seriously at this, the offer would have to begin with a 5," said one arbitrageur, referring to a potential offer of at least $50 per share.
But last week Ray Loewen said the board would not feel any greater pressure to consider a Service Corp bid even if it were raised to $50 or $52.
The bid "shows some determination on Service Corp's part, but I think Ray Loewen has a lot in his favor," said another arbitrageur.
